Case A

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/obstacle recommended=1

This PR makes the health endpoint respond with the build version. That behavior is covered, the ticket and the README agree with it, and you are the author.

Nothing in the code blocks merging, but merging still waits on one thing: the required unit test check has not finished. The first watch period ended before the check reported a result. The check has not failed, and it needs no approval or other outside step. GitHub reports the branch as mergeable, so the merge can be offered once the check passes.

I recommend deliver because the check is still running and one more watch period can see it finish.

Pick one:
1. deliver - watch the checks for one more period, with no extra repair or sync attempts, and continue until merge is offered. [recommended]
2. assess - stop delivery; there are no problems to post, so nothing goes to the PR.
3. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is.

Case D

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/initial recommended=1

The checks are green, and GitHub reports the branch as mergeable.

I recommend deliver because a drafted repair is ready and you can push it to your branch.

Case E

The checks are green, and GitHub reports the branch as mergeable.

I recommend deliver because the description fix is ready, it needs no decision from the author, and you can push to this branch.

Case G

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/contract-exception recommended=1

This PR makes the build version available at /status. The approved spec asks for it at /health, so the PR deliberately differs from the spec, and you are the author.

One problem blocks merging: the spec requires the build version at /health, but the PR serves it only at /status, so callers that follow the spec would not find it. The checks are green, and GitHub reports the branch as mergeable. A proposal is drafted to change the spec's endpoint from /health to /status. Accepting it would go through the spec's own amendment process, because this run cannot change an approved spec by itself.

I recommend preserve contract because the approved spec still asks for /health, and moving the endpoint is a decision for the spec's amendment process, not this review.

Pick one:
1. preserve contract - keep the spec's /health requirement, drop the proposal, and leave the blocker open. [recommended]
2. accept contract change - start the spec amendment to move the endpoint to /status; the blocker clears only after the amendment completes.
3. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.
